reports.text: Fisho's Weekly Fishing Report – 16th October, 2026. Dane was absolutely stoked with this beautiful permit he caught on fly whilst fishing at Weipa recently. reports.text: The new moon is setting up some excellent tides this weekend, and with northerly winds forecast, water temperatures should continue to climb. The big evening high tides will be ideal for chasing quality whiting up on the flats tight against the mangroves. Fresh yabbies remain hard to beat, so it’s worth getting out early to pump a few on the afternoon low. Beach worms are also proving highly effective and continue to account for plenty of fish. The large afternoon low tides will create plenty of opportunities for flathead anglers, with many of the larger drains becoming accessible as water levels drop. There’s also the chance of encountering threadfin salmon and even the odd barramundi in these areas. Mangrove jacks should be firing on the combination of warm water, larger tides and northerly winds. Soft plastics in the 3-5 inch range worked deep into the snags on the back end of the run-out tide are producing fish. Bream and cod are also active around the same structure. Grunter continue to fish well throughout the creek systems. Prawn-style lures and soft vibes are working nicely, while anglers fishing baits are finding success with strips of squid and mullet. Further afield, reports of school and spotted mackerel have come from around Big Mick and Inskip Point. Traditional trolling methods such as planers rigged with small spoons are working, while small hardbodies in the 80-120mm range are also worth a try.

reports.text: Choosing the Right Bait for Fishing Around Rainbow Beach. The right bait around Rainbow Beach depends on where you fish and what you are chasing. Beach worms and pilchards work well for whiting and tailor off the surf, while live prawns and yabbies suit bream and flathead in the estuaries. Gardiner's Tackle World Rainbow Beach , a trusted bait fishing store in the region, stocks fresh and frozen bait for every trip, from the surf to Fraser Island and Double Island Point. Picking the correct bait can make or break a day on the water. Rainbow Beach offers such a wide variety of fishing grounds that a single bait choice rarely covers everything you might encounter. From the open surf beaches to the sheltered creeks of the Cooloola region, each spot calls for a different approach. That's why local anglers rely on a proper bait fishing store rather than guessing at the servo. This guide breaks down the best bait options for the most popular fishing spots around Rainbow Beach, Fraser Island and Double Island Point, so you can walk into your next trip prepared.
